You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like early 2025. Fed funds at 4.33 means the Fed has been on hold since December 2024, and the 12m change of -1.00 fits the cuts made in late 2024. Gold up 40% over 12 months fits March 2025 or a month near it.

The unemployment rate is 4.0%, though, and headline CPI at 3.0% with core at 3.29% doesn't fit early 2025. Those numbers look more like a later month.

Fed funds at 4.33 could also hold from the December 2024 cut through August 2025. In September 2025 the rate was cut to 4.09–4.33, which would put the effective rate near 4.1. A 3m change of -0.25 would then mean a cut within the last three months, which points to the effective rate of about 4.33 before September. That doesn't match.

Another candidate is early 2025 with January 2025 CPI at 3.0% headline and core at 3.3%. January 2025 headline CPI was 3.0% and core was 3.3%, a good match. But unemployment in January 2025 was 4.0%, which also matches. The 3m change in the policy rate of -0.25 fits the December 2024 cut, and the 12m change of -1.00 fits too, since the rate was 5.33 in January 2024.

The 2-year yield at 4.07 is a bit low for January 2025, which was near 4.2–4.3, and the 10-year at 4.29 is low for the month, which ended near 4.54. The 10-year at 4.29 with the 2-year at 4.07 fits the end of February 2025: the 10-year was 4.21 and the 2-year 3.99. The VIX at 21 and equities -1.3% for the month also fit February 2025. Payrolls averaged 237k, which fits a window that includes the strong December and November readings. Treasuries 20y+ up 5.4% in a month fits February 2025. Core CPI for February was 3.1% and headline 2.8%, so January's 3.0% and 3.3% remain the better fit. But CPI is the latest published, and by end of February, January CPI would be the latest. So February 2025.
